clue.text: Bat around wicket heading glances away from cover

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word glances off and departs, leaving the rest behind

blocks.note: W is the scorecard abbreviation for a wicket
a gander is a look or glance, as in 'take a gander'

explanation.surface: A batsman shuffles about as the bowler comes round the wicket and his shots glance away from the cover fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture (round the wicket, a glance, cover) is all disguise. W plus GANDER without its first letter gives WANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To bat around is informal for roaming aimlessly from place to place, which is what it means to wander.

clue.text: Hero's cross, mostly open up-front

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
up front means at the head of the line, so that piece is placed first

blocks.note: a door left slightly open is ajar
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A hero is cross, and openly shows it from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up-front' places the shortened word before the cross; 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax is a warrior of Greek legend who fought at Troy, so a mythic hero.

clue.text: Budget papers boosted feverish chapter

indicators.note: in a down entry, boosted means pushed upwards, so the word reads bottom to top
something feverish is agitated and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: ID papers are identity documents
taken as written

explanation.surface: Budget documents were rushed out with a hurried extra chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: Budget as an adjective means low-priced, the same as very cheap goods or deals.

clue.text: Maybe rat's lair beset by decay

indicators.note: something beset is surrounded on all sides, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: rot is decay
a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: A rat's home is falling apart with rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks the rat as one example of the class; 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is one example of a rodent, the gnawing mammal order that also includes mice.

clue.text: Drying-room pipe that's 25.4 microns internally

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so one part sits within the other

blocks.note: a hose is a flexible pipe
a thou is a thousandth of an inch, which is 25.4 microns

explanation.surface: Describes a drying-room's pipework with an oddly precise engineering measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: The exact figure is the giveaway: a thousandth of an inch is 25.4 microns, and engineers call it a thou.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothouse is a heated room or glasshouse, and heated rooms were used for drying things.

clue.text: What attracts sick hatemongers outside Oxford?

indicators.note: sick suggests something unwell and out of order, so the letters are rearranged
outside means wrapped around, so the rearranged letters surround the other part

blocks.note: taken as written
an Oxford is a style of laced leather shoe

explanation.surface: Asks what draws ill-tempered bigots to gather outside Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford looks like the city or university; it is a style of shoe, which sits in the middle of the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped magnet pulls iron towards it, so it is literally a thing that attracts.

clue.text: Article on Charlie Parker's film

blocks.note: the definite article
Charlie Parker, the jazz saxophonist, was nicknamed Bird; with the 's that makes Bird's

explanation.surface: A write-up about a biopic of the jazz saxophonist Charlie Parker.
explanation.walkthrough: Parker's nickname was Bird, and the possessive 's supplies the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Birds is Hitchcock's 1963 thriller in which flocks attack a Californian town, a well-known film.

clue.text: D-Day objective that's now clear following order

indicators.note: following means coming behind, so the exclamation goes after the other piece

blocks.note: OM is the Order of Merit
aha is what you say when something becomes clear

explanation.surface: A military target whose purpose becomes plain once orders are given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the exclamation after the order. OM is the British Order of Merit.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha was the code name for one of the Normandy landing beaches assigned to American troops in June 1944.

clue.text: It'll emerge from sulphur left in furrow overwhelmed by poo

definitions.text: It'll emerge from sulphur left in furrow overwhelmed by poo

indicators.note: in places one item inside the next word, here at its front
to be overwhelmed is to be swamped on every side, so the inner group is enclosed

blocks.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
a mess, as a dog might leave
L is the abbreviation for left
a furrow is a line, as on a brow

explanation.surface: A stench rising from a trench of sulphur fouled with excrement.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a reek is what comes off sulphur and dung.
explanation.definitionFit: Sulphur compounds and excrement both stink, so a bad odour is exactly what emerges from them.

clue.text: American workforce embracing impressive US dog

indicators.note: embracing means hugging something within, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: labour in its American spelling, the workforce
rad is American slang for impressive or cool

explanation.surface: American workers fawning over a fine US dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces carry an American flag: the spelling without the U, and the slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Labrador is a breed of retriever, a popular family dog originally from Newfoundland.

clue.text: Procrastinator shuns Germany in high-level 13

indicators.note: to shun is to avoid, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: someone who delays
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A dawdler avoids Germany while stuck in some lofty region.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 points to the answer at 13-across, ZONE, so the definition is a high zone.
explanation.definitionFit: The E layer is a band of the ionosphere about 100 km up, a high-altitude region of the atmosphere.

clue.text: Innately study info linked to large country houses

indicators.note: something that houses another holds it within

blocks.note: to con is to study or pore over
gen is British slang for information
a European country
L is the clothing size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Studying details about large country houses seems to come naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country houses' looks like stately homes; country is the nation and houses is the instruction to enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: Something present congenitally is there from birth, which is what innate means.

clue.text: Closely pursuing dodgy exploits at No.1 after release of fake pix

indicators.note: dodgy means suspect and unreliable, so the letters are rearranged
releasing letters lets them go, so they are removed from the group first

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
the digit 1 looks like the letter I
fake signals these three letters can be found in any order

explanation.surface: Tabloid tale of shady deeds by a top star after fake photos are released.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P, I and X from the letters of exploits at No.1, then rearrange the ten that remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Following nose to tail means one directly behind another, tightly tailing the leader.

clue.text: Working after turning north, back from Bible belt

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the working piece follows the turned letter
back points to the rear end, so only the final letter is used

blocks.note: the letter N turned on its side looks like a Z
a machine that is working is on
the final letter of Bible

explanation.surface: A worker heading north and away from the American Bible Belt.
explanation.walkthrough: A visual trick: rotate N a quarter turn and it becomes Z. 'Bible belt' reads as one phrase, but belt is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt is a region or area, as in a commuter belt, the same as a zone.

clue.text: Bundling, say, Roy and Heather together

blocks.note: Roy Hudd was a British comedian and radio presenter
ling is common heather

explanation.surface: Roy and Heather snuggling together, as in the old practice of bundling.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy and Heather look like a couple's names; 'say' asks for the surname of a famous Roy, and heather is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bundling, crowding together in a tight group, is a sense of huddling.

clue.text: Liberal ideas shocked mum's new Lothario

indicators.note: shocked suggests being jolted out of place, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
taken as written
ma is an informal word for mum
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Mum is scandalised by the permissive views of her new womaniser boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario, a seducer in an 18th-century play, became the byword for a man who chases women.

clue.text: Design fine publicity I will shortly read out

indicators.note: reading something out means saying it, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
to give something an airing is to publicise it
I will contracted is I'll, said the same as a small island

explanation.surface: Promises to read out a short, fine piece of publicity about a design.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair Isle is a knitting pattern of coloured bands, named after a Shetland island, so a design.

clue.text: Bound to incorporate map for rapid transport

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take in as part of the body, so one part goes inside

blocks.note: a jeté is a ballet leap
a plan is a map or drawing

explanation.surface: A map is sure to be included when arranging fast travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' looks like 'certain to'; Bound is the ballet leap, jeté.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet plane is a jet-engined aircraft, a fast means of transport.

clue.text: I've been stupid about beginning to save money

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one part wraps round the other
the beginning is the first letter only

blocks.note: doh is the cry of someone realising they have been dim
the first letter of save

explanation.surface: Someone kicks themselves for failing to put money aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosh is British slang for money or cash.

clue.text: He's committed to see AC/DC on grass

blocks.note: AC/DC is slang for bisexual, shortened to bi
to grass on someone is to inform, or shop them

explanation.surface: A rock fan who is determined to catch AC/DC playing an open-air gig.
explanation.walkthrough: AC/DC looks like the rock band. In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a diocese, and a bishop is the cleric appointed to lead it.

clue.text: Right – not, vice versa, wrong

indicators.note: wrong means incorrect, so the letters are put in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A playful argument: right isn't wrong, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vice versa' wants to be an instruction to reverse; it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Right in politics is the conservative wing, so the word stands for a conservative.

clue.text: Flower stems, section of Turk's Cap, identified

indicators.note: a section is a slice from a longer piece, so the letters lie within the words

blocks.note: the letters run from the possessive S through the next word into the first letter after it

explanation.surface: Stems of the Turk's Cap lily have been identified.
explanation.walkthrough: Turk's Cap is a lily, so the surface stays in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Scapi is the plural of scape, a botanist's term for a leafless flowering stalk.

clue.text: Judge's first question covering promotion

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the pair goes outside the other part

blocks.note: Q is the abbreviation for question
an ad promotes a product
first is one, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A judge's opening question touches on someone's career promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A qadi is a judge in an Islamic court, applying sharia law.

clue.text: Songs of Praise in España translated

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the Spanish name for Spain, ignoring the tilde

explanation.surface: The BBC hymn programme Songs of Praise is dubbed for Spanish viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: Songs of Praise is a long-running BBC Sunday programme of hymn singing, but here it is a plain description.
explanation.definitionFit: A paean is a song or hymn of praise or triumph, originally to Apollo.

clue.text: Book half a hotel on 3rd and 4th of June

indicators.note: ordinal positions pick out exactly those letters from the word

blocks.note: the third and fourth letters of June
hemi- is the prefix for half
taken as written
H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Booking half a hotel for the third and fourth of June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb about reserving rooms; it is the noun. In an across clue 'on' places the hotel part after the June letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nehemiah is a book of the Old Testament describing the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.

clue.text: Most obvious nuisance, note, among cuts

indicators.note: to cut into something is to go inside it, so these letters split the other word

blocks.note: a pest is a nuisance
la is a note of the sol-fa scale
in means among

explanation.surface: Of all the cuts, the clearest is the nuisance flagged in a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' looks like a noun, as in spending cuts; it is the verb telling the note and 'among' to cut into the nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means clear or evident, so the superlative plainest is the most evident.

clue.text: Arbitrary number checked by sharp staff includes one small digit

indicators.note: to be checked is to be held back or hemmed in, so this goes inside
includes means holds within, so another letter is placed inside

blocks.note: a pike is a long staff with a sharp point
n stands for an unspecified number in algebra
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A random number checked by a sharp staffer contains a tiny digit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digit' looks numerical, but it means a finger here. The weapon holds both letters, N after its first two letters and I after the K.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinkie is the little finger, the smallest digit of the hand.
